difficulty.from: engine meta: the only cube in the answer is hidden

answer.line: Only one cube has exactly one painted side, and you cannot see it: the bottom cube in the middle of the back row.

steps: Know the paint rule: every exposed side is painted except the bottom. That includes the two back sides you cannot see, the ones facing upper left and upper right in the drawing.
Count floor by floor, bottom up, and write each cube's number of painted sides. The floor maps in the picture do this for you.
One cube has exactly one: the bottom cube in the middle of the back row, under the tall tower. Neighbors cover its top and three sides; only the side facing upper right is open.
Hidden cubes count. Any cube holding up a cube you can see is really there.

choices.note: The hidden cube under the tower, its upper-right side painted.
Leave out the hidden sides facing upper right and 2 cubes come out with one painted side. Those back sides get paint too.
Leave out the hidden sides facing upper left and 3 cubes come out with one painted side. Hidden sides still get paint.
Count only the top and the two front sides you can see, and 4 cubes show exactly one. The rule counts every exposed side but the bottom.
No single slip gives 5 here. Recount floor by floor and write each cube's number down.

lockIt: Paint every exposed side but the bottom, count floor by floor, and count the hidden cubes that hold others up.
